segments.note: First section of the Pittsburgh, Virginia and Charleston (Monongahela Valley Railroad until Feb 1870), opened November 1872 from the PV&C's own station at 4th & Tye Streets, South Pittsburgh, via Twelfth Street, Nineteenth Street (Birmingham), Ormsby (Thirtieth St), Beck's Run and Hays to Homestead (WIKI; BLUK shows South Pittsburg, Ormsby, Hay's and Homestead in the 1875 Official Guide). The PV&C ran its own trains until the Pennsylvania Railroad took over 'control and management' in May 1879 (CRUMRINE; ELLIS) - the PRR's stock control from Nov 1872 did not change who ran the trains. Continued from 1879 as the PRR feature prr-mon-south-side-elrama. headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no timetable frequency from this era was read.

metadata.operator_split: May 1879: the PV&C ran its own trains 1872-1879; the Pennsylvania Railroad operated the line under lease from May 1879 (Crumrine; Ellis; Wikipedia). PV&C features end 1879 and PRR features sharing their geometry begin 1879. NOT splits: PRR stock control from Nov 1872 (stock purchase); the 1 Apr 1905 merger into the PRR (operator unchanged). Everything south of Monongahela City opened under PRR operation.
metadata.colour_note: PRR colour #7B241C pulled programmatically from data/pennsylvania_railroad.geojson and confirmed identical on every feature with company 'Pennsylvania Railroad' in data/. PV&C colour #5695BF is new; no company in data/ used it (checked programmatically 2026-10-22).
